correctness.rationale: All essential theorems verified independently. Lemma 1 (column disjointness, sum w_i(w_i-1)<=n(n-1)) checked: if two rows share j and l!=j then J2, sets F_i\{j} disjoint, summation correct. Lemma 2 (weight-1 peeling, rank>=rank(C)+1): restriction argument kills e_n, C inherits diagonal-ones/J2 as principal submatrix; column case by transpose; verified. Lemma 3 (weight-2 peeling, rank>=rank(E0)+1): row0={0,1} forces row1 avoids 0 else share {0,1}; E0 inherits diagonal/J2; independence via zero block on E0 columns; verified. Theorem A hand lower bounds: r2 det 1 on 3 matrices; r3 weight-1 expansion det 1 plus all>=2 forces (2,2,2) via 2+2+6=10>6 counting, no 2-cycles so 3-cycles det 2; r4 weight-1 gives 1+r3, weight-2 gives 1+r2, else 4*6=24>12 impossible; r5 weight-1 gives 1+r4=4, weight-2 gives 1+r3=4, else 5*6=30>20 impossible; residues and induction valid; upper bounds by Theorem B construction. Re-ran enumerate.py: n=2 total 4 survivors 3 min 2 dist {2:3}; n=3 total 64 survivors 21 min 3; n=4 total 4096 survivors 311 min 3 dist {3:6,4:305}; n=5 total 1048576 survivors 8995 min 4 dist {4:390,5:8605} in ~3s, exactly matching DRAFT. Cross-checked Bareiss rank vs Fraction exact rank on tilings n=4,5,8,12 and all n=4 survivors and 2000 random n=5: all match, no float tolerance. Verified every n=4 survivor has nonsingular 3x3 minor and every n=5 survivor has nonsingular 4x4 minor by independent find_minor on same matrix (bad=0 both). Verified minimizer CSVs: 6 rows n=4 all diag-ones J2-free rank 3; 390 rows n=5 all rank 4. Verified orbit counts: n=4 minimizers 1 orbit size 6 (all directed 4-cycles, (4-1)!=6); n=5 minimizers 5 orbits sizes 120,120,60,60,30 sum 390; survivor orbits 107 sum 8995. Verified weight-multiset n=3 split (1,2,2)x9,(1,1,2)x6,(1,1,3)x3,(2,2,2)x2,(1,1,1)x1 dets 1x19,2x2. Theorem B: 4-cycle block supports {a,b},{b,c},{c,d},{d,a} pairwise intersections 1 (adjacent) or 0 (opposite), across blocks 0, block-diagonal J2-free; dependency ra+rc-rb-rd=0 so rank<=3, top-left 3x3 det 1 so exactly 3; total 3*floor(n/4)+(n mod 4)=ceil(3n/4) checked residues 0..3; re-ran construct_upper n=2..12 exact ranks match target. Theorem C: weight<=2 characterization f with no 2-cycles verified (weight-1 rows never cause J2 since size 1; weight-2 pair shares 2 iff equal 2-sets iff 2-cycle); weight-1 case 1+ceil(3(n-1)/4)>=ceil(3n/4) checked residues, C preserves weight<=2; leaf indegree-0 gives column weight 1, C preserves weight<=2 since no one points to leaf; indegree>=1 with sum n forces indegree 1 everywhere so disjoint cycles length>=3 (no fixed points, no 2-cycles), block-diagonal I+P; det(I+P)=1-(-1)^L via lambda^L-1 at -1 gives 2 if L odd (full rank) and 0 if L even with alternating null vector and (L-1)x(L-1) triangular det 1 so rank L-1; L-1>=3L/4 for even L>=4 equality only at 4, L>=3L/4 for odd L; sum >=3n/4 plus integer rounding gives ceil; base n=1 holds. Computationally re-verified weight<=2 exhaustive n=6 valid 28821 min 5, n=7 valid 505876 min 6, n=8 exhaustive 16M valid 10270569 min 6 matching ceil(3n/4). Theorem D: Frobenius rank(G)>= (tr G)^2/||G||_F^2 via Cauchy on eigenvalues, G=MM^T diag w_i off-diag 0/1, denominator Sr+2P=Sr+Sc-W with P=sum C(c_j,2) (each intersecting pair in exactly one column by J2-free) verified; need Sr+Sc<=2W^2/n+W, coarse KST Sr-W<=n(n-1), Sc-W<=n(n-1) gives Sr+Sc<=2W+2n(n-1), suffices W+2n(n-1)<=2W^2/n i.e. 2W^2-Wn-2n^2(n-1)>=0 increasing in W (4W-n>0), minimal W=3n gives n^2(17-2n)>=0 true for n<=8 (n=8 gives 64>0); light row/column peeling ratios 1+ceil((n-1)/2)>=ceil(n/2) and 1+ceil((n-2)/2)>=ceil(n/2) checked even/odd; n=6 all>=3 impossible via 6n>n(n-1); sequential induction 6 then 7 then 8 valid. No overclaim: general n/2 only to n<=8, full 3n/4 as Conjecture E with heuristic support, clearly separated. One non-decisive presentation defect: minors_n5.csv writes canonical rep c but minor rows/cols/det for different member M in same orbit (export_csv.py lines 119-120), so literal check of minor on displayed rep fails (e.g. orbit 19 det 2 vs 1 on rep; orbit 98 minor singular on rep). Underlying existence claim is TRUE by independent per-matrix check (bad=0), and hand induction already proves r5>=4 without CSV, so defect does not falsify any theorem; corrected in RESULT artifacts.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval confirms no source covers or implies the candidate when hypotheses, quantifiers, constants and scope are compared, not just keywords. (1) Kovacs (arXiv abstract + API summary inspected): hypothesis is arbitrary binary X, quantifier is equality i(X)=br(X) for all submatrices; Boolean rank allows Boolean sum of rank-1 binaries, fundamentally different from real rank over Q/R via Bareiss; no diagonal fixed to 1 (so zero-matrix trivialization absent), no minimization over F_n, no parameter r(n), no constants 2,3,3,4 or ceil(3n/4), no 4-cycle tiling or Frobenius/KST lower-bound argument. (2) Haviv (arXiv abstract + Crossref journal record inspected, ACM Trans. Comput. Theory 11(4):1-13): hypothesis is any graph G with complement H-free, matrix may use any field entries subject only to diag nonzero and zeros on nonedges; quantifier is max_G min_M rank, yielding asymptotic Omega(sqrt(n)/log n) for K3 and n^delta for non-bipartite H over R; candidate quantifier is min_M rank with all entries pinned to {0,1} and diag pinned to 1 and forbidden pattern is the constant J2 everywhere — Haviv's free-entry construction cannot be specialized to 0/1 diagonal-ones J2-free matrices and gives no small-n exact values, no 6/390 minimizer classification, no 3-vs-4 residue-specific 4-cycle construction with rank exactly 3 per block. (3) Parnas-Shraibman (arXiv abstract inspected): hypothesis fixes real rank d in 1..4, conclusion bounds binary/Boolean rank above by small constants and characterizes (2d-2)-size extremal circulants; candidate hypothesis fixes combinatorial class F_n and concludes real rank itself is minimized, with exact table and general ceil(3n/4) vs ceil(n/2) bounds — directions are dual and neither implies the other; their extremal matrices are not diagonal-ones J2-free minimizers. Exact-phrase arXiv searches for C4-free+rank, diagonal-ones+J2-free, minimum-real-rank+diagonal, and C4-free+real-rank all returned 0 hits; Crossref fuzzy searches for the full objective and for ceil(3n/4) returned only irrelevant top hits (NIST rank tests, infrared spectra, Seliverstov diagonal-rank bounds which concern lower bounds for matrices with 0/1 outside diagonal without J2 restriction and contain no r(n) table). Therefore this documented search found no substantive covering prior art.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later, not textbook/parameter/tiny-gain/unexplained enumeration. Defines new natural extremal problem (C4-free bipartite condition plus diagonal-ones normalization; without normalization zero matrix trivializes) linking forbidden-pattern combinatorics to rank rigidity/minrank/biclique-cover context. Provides first exact values r(2)=2,r(3)=3,r(4)=3,r(5)=4 with human-checkable inductions plus machine certificates (counts, 1 and 5 minimizer orbits, 107 survivor orbits, explicit nonsingular minors) - explained catalog, not raw table: weight-multisets, canonical forms, J2/rank verification. Provides general theorems for all n: ceil(3n/4) upper bound by explicit 4-cycle block-diagonal tiling (non-obvious 3/4 ratio emerging from 4-cycles) and matching lower bound proving tiling optimal among all row-weight<=2 matrices via leaf+cycle induction - infinite-family result, not just small n. Extends general lower bound ceil(n/2) to n<=8 via peeling+Frobenius+KST with honest open step for n>=9 all>=3 and sharp conjecture r(n)=ceil(3n/4) supported by exhaustive weight<=2 to n=8 and heuristic to n=12, clearly separating theorem vs conjecture. Small-n table plus sharp tiling plus sparse optimality plus conjecture forms coherent reference point for future C4-free rank work; rediscovery would merit recording. Rejects textbook restatement (no textbook contains this table/bound), mere substitution (new objective/normalization), tiny gain (3/4 vs 1/2 gap is substantive, sparse optimality is tight), unexplained enumeration (grouped orbits+minors+hand proofs).
